text:
alex: FYI — nsight run on ded-02 shows a ~12% p99 spike after yesterday's batching heuristic change. nvtx timeline has a bunch of tiny ranges around the prefetch handoff. uploaded raw trace to perf-bot.
perf-bot: New profile uploaded: s3://perf.redwood/nsys/2187654321/ded-02.nsys
maria: Link please? summary of suspected root cause? kernel selector or kv-cache flush?
alex: Looks like kernel_selector is toggling prefetch -> kernel_B path and we get an extra memcpy + synchronize. nvtx shows a 'handoff' span nested inside the request span that lines up with the memcpy.
sam: Can we make ranges per-request like `req/<id>/kernel-handoff` so traces group cleanly? current names are ambiguous when we aggregate.
jordan: +1 conceptually, but creating per-request ranges at high QPS can blow up nvtx overhead. We should combine with sampling or reduce frequency.
ryan: Alternative: keep coarse ranges for hot kernels and add lightweight tags via nvtxRangePushEx or nvtxDomain metadata. That lets dashboards group without huge range churn.
maria: Is the memcpy happening on CPU? nsight timeline shows memcpy ops on stream 2 while kernel_B launches on stream 1.
alex: Confirmed — memcpy + cudaStreamSynchronize in selector_common.cpp:prefetch_handoff(). I suspect a blocking flush of small KV entries.
sam: Quick patch idea — defer flush to an async worker and mark nvtxRange as 'handoff-async'. Pseudo:
```c
nvtxRangePushA("req:%s/handoff-async", req_id);
enqueue_prefetch(req);
nvtxRangePop();
```
That avoids sync in fast path.
jordan: Pattern looks fine; add bounded queue to avoid unbounded memory growth. Also instrument only 1/10 requests for detailed spans to limit NVTX volume.
alex: Ran a microbench with mock async handoff — p99 dropped from 210ms -> 182ms, steady throughput similar. Uploading diffs shortly.
perf-bot: Differential report: https://perf.redwood/compare/2187654321 — shows kernel_B stalls reduced and fewer stream sync events.
ryan: Naming convention proposal: top-level request span: `redwood.req.<short-id>.<phase>`; kernel ranges: `kernel:<model>:<variant>:seq<len>`; handoff range: `handoff:<type>`; keep names under 64 chars to match telemetry backend limits.
maria: +1. Also prefix NVTX labels used by dashboards with `nvtx:route:` so parsing rules are stable.
alex: Action items: (1) sam prototype async handoff + bounded queue (2) jordan add sampling instrumentation (3) ryan draft nvtx naming doc/PR (4) alex run 3 nsight runs and post results.
sam: Taking (1). will push WIP PR today.
jordan: Taking (2). default 1/20 sampling and an env var to override.
ryan: I'll draft the naming doc under eng-runtime/instrumentation-guides and include examples.
alex: Thanks all — if anyone hits regressions after the change, ping @here and paste the nvtx snippet. :thumbsup:
